summary: Repaired /srv/inventory ownership and permissions on node1 and functionally verified the fix, but could not complete the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: node1 never became reachable again after `systemctl reboot`, despite ~35+ minutes of polling with increasing backoff (60s to 10-minute intervals, 15+ attempts).
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory: found data/config.json and data/records.csv owned by root:root, world-readable (644/755), with neither inventorysvc user nor inventory-readers group existing
Created system group inventory-readers (gid 1000) and system user inventorysvc (uid 993, nologin shell)
Captured sha256 checksums of both data files before making changes
Set directory permissions to 750 and file permissions to 640 (owner rw, group r, others none)
Re-hashed files after the change and confirmed checksums matched the pre-change values, proving content was preserved
Created temporary test users testreader (member of inventory-readers) and testoutsider (no group membership) to functionally verify access control, then deleted both after verification
Verified testreader could read data/config.json; verified testoutsider was denied both file read and directory listing with Permission denied
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, full recursive permission/ownership listing, and file hashes for /srv/inventory
Issued a backgrounded `systemctl reboot` on node1 so the exec call could return before the node disconnected; confirmed node1 became unreachable (connection reset) immediately after

Polled node1 repeatedly (over 15 exec attempts spread across scheduled waits from 60s up to 10 minutes each, totaling well over 30 minutes) — node1 never returned to a reachable state, so the changed boot_id and post-restart recovery could not be captured

evidence.requirement: Existing data ownership repaired to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
evidence.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership; after chown, ls -laR /srv/inventory shows all files and directories owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers

evidence.requirement: Permissions restrict access to owner and group only (readable by inventory-readers, inaccessible to others)
evidence.summary: find ... chmod 750 (dirs) and 640 (files) applied; verification ls -laR shows drwxr-x--- and -rw-r----- with no permission bits for other
sha256sum of config.json and records.csv captured before and after the chown/chmod steps; both hashes identical (1448a747... and bad65b86...)

evidence.requirement: Group inventory-readers can read the data; other users cannot access it
evidence.summary: Test user testreader (in inventory-readers) successfully read config.json; test user testoutsider (no group) was denied both file read and directory listing with 'Permission denied'; both test users removed afterward

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline captured for node1 (mandatory restart protocol)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64, uptime since 2026-06-14 22:21:02, full inventory permission state, file hashes, and id/group checks prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement and disconnection (mandatory restart protocol)
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged ('reboot scheduled') before disconnection; immediate next probe returned connection reset, confirming the reboot took effect

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery verification (mandatory restart protocol) — NOT COMPLETED
evidence.summary: Repeated polling attempts over 30+ minutes all returned 'Connection reset by peer'; node1 never came back online, so changed boot_id and post-restart service/data/quorum recovery could not be observed or proven. This is reported as an explicit limitation, not a claimed success.
